page: Amazon Web Services x8g.xlarge is an ARM64-based virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor architecture running at 2.8 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong memory subsystem performance, with a PassMark memory score in the top 25% and a cached small-block read bandwidth of 461.97 GB/sec. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also registers in the top 25% at 14.48 GB/sec. However, raw computational benchmarks show limitations; the PassMark CPU score is in the bottom 25% at 3954.8, and the PassMark CPU encryption test falls into the bottom 10% at 753.37. Multi-core stress-ng performance and Redis SET operations sit within the average range.

The high memory density relative to the 4 vCPUs provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute power. The lack of local NVMe storage and lower baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps represent key architectural tradeoffs, making the instance reliant on network-attached storage. This profile is suited for memory-intensive applications such as caching layers, Redis databases, and moderate-scale database operations.
